title: No-show handling with a first-night fee
description:
Guests who never arrive currently keep their reservation `CONFIRMED` forever: the whole stay stays booked (nobody can sell the remaining nights) and the full charge is kept. Front desks asked for the usual no-show rule: keep the first night, refund the rest, free the rooms.

- New status `NO_SHOW` (migration V2 widens `reservation_status_check`).
- A reservation still `CONFIRMED` once the property's check-out time on the day after its check-in date has passed, in the property's own zone (`Reservation.noShowFrom()`), is a no-show. Before that moment marking it is a 409.
- The fee is the stored price lines of the first night (the room-night line, which covers every room of the reservation, plus that night's extra-guest line), capped at the total. Stay-level lines such as the length-of-stay discount are not counted. The rest of the total, if any, is refunded through `PaymentGateway` with the key `no-show-<reservation id>` and recorded as a `REFUND` ledger entry with reason `no-show`.
- Inventory: `booked` goes down by the reservation's rooms for every night from the second one on, in ascending order like the other inventory writes; the first night stays booked.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/reservations/{reference}/no-show` returns the reservation with `feeAmount`, `refundAmount` and `currency`.
- The maintenance job marks no-shows on every run (`BookingMaintenanceJob.markNoShows`, `noShows` in the maintenance report). It reads candidate ids in pages (`status = CONFIRMED and check_in <= today's UTC date`, enough since no zone is a whole day ahead of UTC), and each stay is its own transaction that re-reads it and checks the exact moment in its zone. Like cancel, the reservation row is flushed before inventory moves, so a concurrent check-in, cancel or second no-show loses on the version and the optimistic retry turns it into a conflict (or, for the job, a skip): money moves once. Marking waits at most `booking.lock-timeout` for each row lock, like hold release and expiry: the transaction sets `lock_timeout` for itself only (`set_config(..., true)`), through a small `LockWaits` component extracted from `HoldService.lockedGetWithinTimeout`, which now uses it too. The staff route then answers 503 `busy`. A stay the job cannot close in this run, whatever the failure (a declined refund, a row still locked after the timeout, a race it keeps losing, a database error: any `RuntimeException` from that stay's unit of work), is rolled back, skipped and logged at WARN with its reservation id and the exception class only; the cursor moves past it, so later stays are still marked and the rest of the report is returned, and the next run tries it again under the same `no-show-<reservation id>` refund key.
- Note on rollout: the rule applies to every confirmed stay whose guest never arrived, also those booked before this change, so the first job run after deploying closes those too and refunds all but their first night. The README says so.
- The log line names the reservation id and the amounts, never the reference.

Tests: service (too early refused, fee and refund for a weekend stay, nights released, no check-in/cancel/second mark afterwards, job marks only due stays and only once, a declined refund skips that stay and the job marks the others, then marks it on the next run, a stay whose inventory row another transaction keeps locked is skipped within the timeout and marked once the lock is gone, any other failure for one stay (the test gateway throwing `IllegalStateException`) skips only that stay, log content; the test payment gateway gets `failNextRefund()` and `failNextRefundWith(...)`) and API (route, ledger entry, summary count, admin token, maintenance report). README updated (concepts and API table).
